Parchments unlock as you complete quests. Each one reveals a little more of what the Isle of the East is, and of what the Last Elder truly was.

\"You who sail here, know this. I am the last living student of the old School of the Ancients. My tutors are silent stones. What I have learned, I offer to those brave enough to walk the isle. Read gently. Some of what waits below is not meant to be woken.\"
Given by Rowan upon your first landing.
I.a: The Coastline Was Once Kept

\"The tide pools around the quay aren\'t natural. They were carved. Someone lined them with dressed stone. The stones are older than any temple I have visited on the mainland, and their edges are true to the square, the way old work rarely is. The isle was inhabited long before it was forgotten.\"
Rowan writes this after your first clears of the Shores.

\"The mythrite you brought me is not natural ore. Its grain is too even, its colour too consistent. It reads as if it was grown, not formed. My grandmother taught me a rhyme: \'the isle builds the isle back, stone by patient stone.\' I never understood it. I am starting to.\"
Rowan writes this after receiving her mythrite cache.

\"The tidepool crab you prepared has a taste I remember only from a single fish my grandmother once served. She called it \'a scale off the ancient shore.\' She would not say more. The isle\'s food is not just old. It is the same food, in the same shapes, kept somehow.\"
Rowan\'s kitchen notes after your banquet preparations.
II.a: The Grove Was a Garden

\"The roots grow in rows. The trees are the same trees, spaced exactly, tended by no one. This grove was a garden, someone\'s garden, and whoever tended it left their tools where they last rested. They\'re still sharp.\"
Rowan\'s notes after your Forest clears.
II.b: A Ritual for Not Dying

\"The library\'s oldest text describes a rite its writers called the Grand Ritual. It promised that those who performed it would not die. It does not say they would live. There is a difference. The text does not go on. I am not sure I want it to.\"
Recovered once you help Rowan shore up the library.
II.c: The Order That Bore the Ritual

\"They called themselves the Ancients. Not as a title of age, but of station: those who came first, and those who would still be here when everyone else was gone. Your Coastal regalia matches an illustration on the second wall. The measurements are identical. They wore what you wear now.\"
Rowan compares your first Coastal regalia to the library plates.
III.a: The Peak Was Their Altar

\"The summit is a ring. The ring is a seal. The stones of the ring are not carved. They are named. Each stone is one of the Ancients. There are hundreds of stones. That was, I think, once the whole order.\"
Rowan\'s map after your Peak clears.

\"Your Voidsteel and the seal\'s stones are the same substance. The Ancients bound themselves with what they quarried here. They literally cast their names into the alloy. This is how you contain something that will not stop wanting to live: you write your own name against its name, and hold.\"
Rowan compares Voidsteel ore to a shard of the seal.
III.c: The One Who Would Not Lie Down

\"Every Ancient walked to the ring and lay down as a stone. Every Ancient but one. The last of them refused, and so the others bound that one inside the seal instead of joining it. His stone would have been carved \'Merren.\' It\'s the same word my grandmother would sometimes say in her sleep, and never in the day.\"
Rowan reads to you from the sealing site\'s ledger.

\"The caldera below the peak was dry when the seal was cast. It is now filling with sea. The seal is failing not because someone attacks it from the outside, but because the thing inside it has spent every one of the intervening centuries learning the seal\'s shape from within. When it breaks the seal, it breaks it with the seal\'s own hands.\"
Rowan writes this after your descents into the Abyss.

\"The Grand Ritual did not fail. It worked. Those who performed it lived. What it took, in exchange, was everything that made those lives worth living: their names, their kin, their remembered dead. The oldest Ancients were the emptiest. The Last Elder is the oldest of them all. He does not remember he was once Merren, or that Merren once had a granddaughter, or that this granddaughter is standing on this isle right now. Rowan wrote none of this down. She said it to me in one breath.\"
Rowan speaks this once you complete the full Ancient regalia.
IV.c: Epilogue: What You Bring Back

\"He did not know me. He knew my regalia, because he wore it once. He knew the seal, because he made it. When it came apart, when I brought the last of him down, he did what no other Ancient did: he remembered. Not my name. Not his. He remembered the taste of the crab I served him at the peak. My grandmother\'s recipe.\"\n\n\"That was enough. The isle recognises you now. The stones on the peak have one fewer name, and one more. Whatever you build after this is your own story.\"
Rowan\'s final letter after the Last Elder falls.
